summary: Walter Yeeling Evans-Wentz was a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Stanford University, the University of Oxford, Jesus College, Oxford, and the University of Rennes, and was a disciple of Kazi Dawa Samdup (~1919-1922).
Walther Eidlitz worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied building engineering at TU Wien (~1911-1914) and studied under his guru Swami Sadananda (~1946-1951).

Walther Heissig worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. After doctoral studies at Vienna and Berlin, and habilitations at Göttingen and Bonn, he taught at Fu Jen Catholic University, Peking University, and the University of Bonn.

Walther Marcus was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Giessen, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Heidelberg University, where he completed his Ph.D. under Christian Bartholomae (~1911-1914).
Walther Michaelis was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber (~1894-1898). He served as director of the Francke Foundations from 1931 to 1935.

Walther Prellwitz worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Adalbert Bezzenberger at the University of Königsberg (Ph.D. ~1882-1885), where he later served as a Privatdozent (1901) and extraordinary professor of comparative linguistics (1924).

Walther Schubring was an Indologist who studied under Ernst Leumann at Strasbourg, and at Munich and Berlin. He held posts at the Royal Library of Berlin and Humboldt University, and held the Indology chair at the University of Hamburg (1920-1951).

Walther Wüst worked in Indology and linguistics. After earning his Ph.D. at the University of Munich, he served there as Privatdozent and dean (1935-1945), and held posts at the Ahnenerbe (1936) and Deutsche Akademie (1943).

Wanda Dynowska worked in religious studies, Indology, and Tibetology, having studied at the University of Lausanne. She served as general secretary of the Polish Theosophical Society (1921) and founded the Indo-Polish Library in 1944.
Wang Pachow worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and sinology. He studied under Tan Yun-shan and served on the teaching and research staff at Visva-Bharati University.

Wannaporn Rienjang is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD at Cambridge. She held positions at the British Museum, the Classical Art Research Centre (2017-2020), Thammasat University (2019), and the University of Oxford (attested 2019-2022).

Warren Crawford Cowgill specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Hermann Fränkel at Stanford and Paul Tedesco and Paul Thieme at Yale (Ph.D.), where he later served as assistant professor from 1956 to 1972.

Warren Lee Todd works in philosophy and Indology. He completed his PhD at Lancaster University under Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad, and also studied under Irina Kuznetsova, Peter Harvey, and traditional teacher Chogye Trichen Rinpoche.

Warrin Ratanamalai is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, where he was supervised by Phra Suthithammanuwat and Phra Srisitthimuni, and also studied under Phra Sudhivorayan and Somjin Sammāpañño.

Waso Harada works in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at Ryukoku and Koyasan universities. He held appointments at Koyasan University, Toseiji, Ryukoku University (attested 1999-2006), and Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2002-2007).

Watari Yanai was a scholar in sinology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1898-1901) and subsequently held a post there from ~1908 to 1926.

Wataru Mori was a scholar in philosophy and other fields. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948-1954) and held posts at Tokyo Medical and Dental University (~1968-1973) and the University of Tokyo (~1973-1989).
Wataru Ryose is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1987 under Minoru Kiyota. He also studied under Genjun Sasaki and Frances Wilson.

Wayne Chandira is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He pursued doctoral studies in religious studies at McMaster University under the supervision of Mark Rowe (attested 2026).

Wayne Proudfoot is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned his Th.M. and Ph.D. at Harvard University. He taught at Fordham University and became Professor of Religion at Columbia University around 1972.
